Subject: Post-call notes — latency & throughput baseline

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap from our side and the numbers you asked for:

- Use case: real-time triage summarization for incoming patient messages (short prompts, avg 120 tokens output).
- Current traffic (prod): ~60 requests/minute during peak (RPS ~1.0), but we expect a holiday spike up to ~250 req/min (~4.2 RPS) for 3 days a year.
- Latency target: p95 under 100ms for in-app flows; average ideally <60ms.
- Concurrency: typical simultaneous active sessions ~8–12, burst to 40 for small windows.
- Model: evaluating open 13B quantized variants; we expect to run a single model family at first.

I attached a simple latency_profile.csv that has our observed latencies from the pilot.

Immediate ask: we need a recommendation on whether Hosted API can meet p95 under 100ms reliably, or if we should plan for Dedicated capacity. Also next steps on procurement timelines (PO / SOW) since we have a compliance review starting next month.

Thanks,
Maya

Hi Maya — great to sync this morning. Short recap + proposed next steps below. I’m copying the data points you shared into a quick checklist so our infra team can size options.

Recap of requirements (confirm if I missed anything):
- p95: target <100ms (goal <60ms)
- sustained load: ~1 RPS (60 rpm), expected peak sustained up to ~4.2 RPS (250 rpm)
- concurrent active sessions: 8–12 normally, burst to 40
- model family: single 13B quantized variant to start
- compliance: SOC-2 evidence + PO/SOW in next 30 days

Quick recommendation (high level):
- Hosted API: likely viable for baseline and moderate spikes if we pair with a low-latency model variant and prefix caching. Pros: fastest time-to-prod, simplified procurement. Cons: less predictable tail latency during sustained high bursts (depends on capacity tier).
- Dedicated: recommended if you require predictable p95 under 60ms at scale, or want strict isolation for compliance/performance SLAs. Pros: reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput. Cons: longer lead time / procurement, higher committed cost.

Next steps I propose:
1) Engineering sizing: if you can share 7-day traffic CSV (hourly) and a sample request/response (we can test with your 13B quantized candidate).
2) In parallel, I’ll put together a 2-option proposal: Hosted projection (with conservative p95 headroom) and Dedicated baseline (single-pool config + burst policy).
3) If Hosted looks tight for p95 <60ms, we’ll sketch a Dedicated fast-fail plan (canary then cutover).

I attached a short "redwood-quickplan.pdf" that outlines the two-option template we use for sizing and procurement timelines.

Availability: I can run a controlled latency test with engineering next Wed/Thu if you can share the traffic sample by EOD Monday.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-quickplan.pdf (pdf)
